sources.use: Edo-period Tokaido context, surviving stone paving and cedar avenue, national historic-site status
Official town relationship among checkpoint, cedar avenue, old-road paving, and Amasake Chaya
Published checkpoint-to-Amasake-Chaya guided-course sequence and approximate two-hour-thirty-minute benchmark
Current Hatajuku-Yamane closure dates, affected paving and milestone, and Prefectural Road 732 detour
K old-road bus relationship through Hatajuku and Amasake Chaya; exact departures remain live information

generalizations: This is a route-choice diagram, not a geographic map; distances, curves, and gradients are not to scale
The roughly two-hour-thirty-minute value is the tourism association's guided-course benchmark from the checkpoint through the old road to Amasake Chaya, not a personal pace guarantee
The sixty-to-ninety-minute short option is a LazyTravel planning range that includes the checkpoint's published approximate forty-five-minute standard visit plus a modest cedar-avenue margin
Tea, checkpoint queues, photography, bus waiting, wet stone, and personal mobility can add substantial time
Bus symbols identify useful current route relationships, not guaranteed departures or an accessibility claim
The Hatajuku-Yamane closure was current on 2026-08-20 and is planned through 2027-01-15; reopening and later conditions require a fresh official check

notes: Full-size labels, the compiled B6 page, and both halves of the 760 px diagram inside a 390 px mobile viewport passed visual review.
